body: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite. However, this outcome-level filtering criterion ignores process quality: trajectories that eventually succeed may still contain inefficient interaction patterns such as repetitive file inspection, unstable tool usage, or delayed modification behavior, all of which become part of the imitation target. We propose TQS (Trajectory Quality Score), a structural scoring framework for coding-agent trajectories that operates directly on trajectory structure, requires no LLM judge, and runs in linear time. TQS characterizes trajectory quality through structural signals organized around structured convergence: information focus, intent--action alignment, and policy dynamics. Using 155,144 successful trajectories from a public open-license corpus, we rank trajectories by TQS and fine-tune coding agents on filtered subsets. Models trained on top-ranked trajectories consistently outperform those trained on random or bottom-ranked subsets on SWE-Bench-Verified. Our results suggest that process-level trajectory quality is an important factor in coding-agent supervision and that structural trajectory filtering provides an effective and scalable alternative to LLM-based data selection.
summaryZh: 针对代码智能体监督微调（SFT）中仅依赖结果过滤的局限性，本文提出了TQS（轨迹质量评分）框架。该框架通过分析交互轨迹的结构特征（如信息聚焦、意图对齐等），在无需大模型参与的情况下实现线性时间复杂度的质量评估。实验表明，使用TQS筛选出的高质量轨迹进行微调，能显著提升代码智能体在SWE-Bench-Verified上的表现，证明了过程质量在智能体训练中的关键作用。
